minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 7, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness at 5:11 p.m., on September 7, 2010, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 1, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury (arrived at 5:20 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Staff Absent:  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

INVOCATION: Council Member Ledesma

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Attorney Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

City Council Minutes  1  September 7, 2010
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

  At the hour of 5:13 p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
  Council reconvened at 6:07 p.m. with four City Council Members present. Council
  Member Schlicht returned at 6:09 p.m.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

  City Attorney Bill Curley announced that he is pleased to report that the Council gave a
  positive response during his review. Staff will post, on the city’s web site, both his and
  the City Manager’s goals and objectives for the coming year so the public will be aware
  of the direction they plan to go in.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Presentation by the Sierra Club’s Orange County Global Warming Committee
  Recognizing the City of Mission Viejo’s Efforts in Enacting Responsible Climate
  Aware Policies and Programs

  Mayor Kelley received the recognition from Laura Jackson of the Sierra Club’s Orange
  County Global Warming Committee.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Dan Avery, M.V.: stated that resident Larry Gilbert appeared before the City Council 258
  times between December of 1989 and February of 2010, to complain about a variety of
  city projects.

  Anna Marie Leyenaar, M.V.: expressed appreciation for all that the city has done to
  support Turf Lane Park. She stated that the property has been an embarrassment for
  years and the residents feel that the city's renovation equates to money well spent.

  Dan Brentzel, M.V.: provided a history on the Turf Lane Park ownership concerns and,
  on behalf of the Timberline Association and the Board of Directors of Timberline HOA,
  he thanked the city for refurbishing the park.

  Wendy Bucknum, M.V.: stated that she is impressed with the street improvements on
  Marguerite and La Paz and she noted that a little bit of dust was worth it. Ms. Bucknum
  thanked the City Council for partnering with the Timberline HOA to avoid litigation and
  to find a positive outcome for all. She also announced that the South Orange County
  Regional Chambers of Commerce will host a City Council Candidate “Meet and Greet”
  at the Laguna Hills Community Center on September 30, 2010, at 5:30 p.m.

  Dr. Bert McCoy, President of the Timberline HOA, M.V.: thanked the Boy Scouts and

City Council Minutes  2  September 7, 2010
   the City of Mission Viejo for pulling together and doing a wonderful job to rehabilitate
  Turf Lane Park.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 6 and 7 were pulled from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as described below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated August 6, 2010, in the amount of $1,129,075.13

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated August 13, 2010, in the amount of $950,715.93

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register dated August 20, 2010, in the amount of $783,127.71

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  Oso/Marguerite Intersection Improvements (CIP 844)

  (1) Approved the easement acquisition agreement with Baja Finisterra Condominium
  Association at a total cost of $70,020 and accept the associated easement deeds; and (2)
  authorized the City Clerk to record the easement deeds in the office of the County
  Recorder.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Kelley

City Council Minutes  3  September 7, 2010
 21.  Measure H

  The following spoke in support of the proposed resolution to oppose Measure H: Ellen
  M. Addonizio, CUSD Board of Directors, M.V.; Robert Reidel, M.V.; Julie Collier, M.V.

  The following presented a written statement in favor of the proposed resolution: Sharon
  Campbell, M.V.

  Mayor Kelley announced that she has also received six emails in opposition to her
  proposal and several in support of the resolution.

  Motion made by Mayor Kelley, seconded by Council Member Schlicht, to adopt
  Resolution 10-50 Opposing the Adoption of Measure H, Which Would Require that the
  Capistrano Unified School District Elect its Trustees by Segregated Trustee Area
  Elections.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

PUBLIC HEARINGS

9.  Use of Supplemental Law Enforcement Services Fund Grant Program

  Paul Catsimanes, Public Services Administrative Manager, presented the staff report.

  Mayor Kelley opened the public hearing at 6:52 p.m. With no requests to speak, Mayor
  Kelley closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  approve the Use for the Supplemental Law Enforcement Services Fund for FY 2010-11.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

OLD BUSINESS

10.  Various Speed Limit Updates

City Council Minutes  4  September 7, 2010
   Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  introduce Ordinance 10-282 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

NEW BUSINESS

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the phraseology on page 7 of the
  August 16, 2010, Minutes. She drew attention to the wording in the third paragraph,
  which states "she believes that she won the lawsuit" against Frank Ury. Council Member
  Schlicht read, for the record, a portion of the court transcript which says that "it appears
  to the court that the petitioner is the prevailing party in this case."

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 16, 2010, as
  presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

6.  City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code

  City Clerk Karen Hamman presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht asked questions about filing requirements for consultants and
  inquired about the redlined staff list for the city’s current filers.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to
  adopt Resolution 10-47 Amending the City of Mission Viejo Conflict of Interest Code.

City Council Minutes  5  September 7, 2010
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

7.  Structural Mitigation Grant Applications for Mission Hospital

  Paul Catsimanes, Public Services Administrative Manager, presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed opposition to the city’s involvement in a grant
  application for a hospital building located in another city.

  City Manager Wilberg explained that Mission Viejo has an adopted Hazard Mitigation
  Plan which is one of the requirements of the grant application. He noted that this is really
  a credit to the City of Mission Viejo for having done that work and that the Mission
  Hospital campus in Laguna Beach will serve the entire South County region.

  Peter Bastone, President and CEO of Mission Hospital, M.V.: stated that it is very
  formidable that Mission Viejo has the ability to apply for this kind of grant. It makes the
  city and the hospital stronger and shows Mission Viejo as a real leader in the region. Mr.
  Bastone thanked the Council for their support.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to (1)
  adopt Resolution 10-48 Authorizing the Filing of a Federal Emergency Management
  Agency (FEMA) Pre-Disaster Mitigation Grant Application for a Structural Mitigation
  Project for Mission Hospital Laguna Beach Campus - Nursing Tower; and (2) adopt
  Resolution 10-49 Authorizing the Filing of a Federal Emergency Management Agency
  (FEMA) Pre-Disaster Mitigation Grant Application for a Structural Mitigation Project for
  Mission Hospital Laguna Beach Campus - Radiographic South Building.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

11.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

12.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  6  September 7, 2010
   Mayor Kelley presented the report.

13.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

14.  SCAG Transportation & Communications Committee (TCC) Report

  Mayor Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

City Attorney’s Report

15.  Ordinance Update of Chapter 11.16 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code
  to Prevent Commercial Use of Residential Property; Particularly Prohibiting
  Marijuana Grow Houses

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: asked how the city would find or investigate a marijuana grow
  house.

  Mr. Curley noted that the ordinance does not allow the city to investigate possible grow
  houses but rather is intended to be an additional enforcement tool after the Sheriff's
  Department discovers this kind of use at a Mission Viejo residence.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  introduce Ordinance 10-283 Amending Chapter 11.16 of Title 11 of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

16.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  7  September 7, 2010
   The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Ledesma

17.  Ordinance update to Section 11.13.015 of Chapter 11.13 of Title 11 of the Mission
  Viejo Municipal Code Authorizing Professional Pest Control Providers to be Issued
  Animal Control Oriented Permits Without City Council Presentation

  Council Member Ledesma presented his report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  introduce Ordinance 10-284 Amending Section 11.13.015 of Chapter 11.13 of Title 11
  of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code Authorizing Professional Pest Control Providers to
  be Issued Animal Control Oriented Permits Without City Council Presentation.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Schlicht

18.  Adoption of a Revolving Door Ordinance

  Council Member Schlicht presented her report. She stated that this matter came to her
  attention because the city wrote a check to Mayor Pro Tem Leckness' business, Kwik
  Kopy Printing. Her purpose in bringing this forward is to stop the Council's positions
  from being exploited for self-enrichment.

  Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: speaking as a resident, he noted that the proponent of the
  proposed ordinance has admitted she hasn’t read the city’s current policy and he finds
  that offensive to him as a taxpayer.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht to direct the City Attorney to draft an
  ordinance for the City Council’s consideration at the next City Council Meeting. The
  motion died for lack of a second.

  By consensus, the City Council directed the City Attorney to analyze the City of San Jose
  ordinance and the city’s current policy and determine if there are deficiencies in the
  City’s current Administrative Regulation

City Council Minutes  8  September 7, 2010
 Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the Quarterly Check Register was not included
in the Agenda. This is an important tool and she would like a copy and for the register to appear
on the next Council Agenda. She also expressed concern that several of the comics engaged in
cheap humor at the recent Comedy Night and it sent the wrong message during a Community of
Character event. Council Member Schlicht asked the City Attorney if formal action is necessary
to remove the Council Lifetime benefits.

City Attorney Curley replied that the Council formally acted to remove the benefit and no further
action is necessary.

Council Member Schlicht discussed the library closure during last year’s Readers’ Festival and
requested that her colleagues join her in reversing the Council’s prior decision to close the
library during future Readers’ Festivals and open this public resource and designated cooling
station. There was no action taken on this request.

Council Member Schlicht stated that she has become aware of the City Clerk’s decision to pick
up and destroy campaign signs in the 2010 election. She feels that this new policy helps the
incumbents and it is a First Amendment Right for candidates to post and retrieve these signs.
She noted that signs were returned to the Candidates in the past and she feels they should be
returned again this election.

City Manager Wilberg responded that he made this decision. In the past, as a courtesy, Code
Enforcement staff did return signs that were illegally posted in the public right of way however,
staff found that the courtesy was being abused by the same people over and over. The decision
was made and the City Clerk has notified all of the Council Candidates up front that illegally
posted signs will be picked up and will not be returned.

Council Member Schlicht reiterated that this policy favors the incumbents. She also stated that
Mayor Kelley, as a Council Candidate, should not be allowed to make any more postings on the
city blog and in doing so, she is using public resources. She announced that she is looking
forward to attending the Diablos Football game in Van Nuys this weekend and Council Member
Schlicht concluded her comments by stating that all she is trying to do is shine a light into city
hall and to stop the status quo and business as usual mentality.

Council Member Ury

Council Member Ury stated that he knows 480 cities that would kill to have Mission Viejo’s
version of status quo. We have an outstanding city that is being run extremely well and that is
more a function of the citizens than the individuals. He stated that Mayor Pro Tem Leckness
summed it up pretty succinctly and made an excellent characterization of how things are going.
Council Member Ury noted that the next few months will be interesting, but at the end of the day
the city is made up of voting residents who put the right people in place to make sure we have
the city that we do.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

City Council Minutes  9  September 7, 2010
 19.  Mission Viejo Business Discount/Coupon Program

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented his report and displayed the Huntington Beach web
  site surfcitysavings.com as a potential model for Mission Viejo's program.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct
  staff to survey the Huntington Beach surfcitysavings.com web site to determine start up
  costs, costs to sustain and maintain such a web based program, and return to the City
  Council with a report.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: None

20.  Potential Replacement for Disbanded Mission Viejo City Chamber

  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented his report.

  Jim Leach, Chairman of Board of the Regional Chamber of Commerce: discussed the
  recent transition in the Chamber, how it is organized and how its new and renewed focus
  will provide more value for the Chamber members.

  Rick Sandzimier, M.V.: stated that he is encouraged by the innovative thinking he’s
  heard tonight and he thanked Dave Leckness for bringing new energy and exploring
  better ways to bring in tax dollars. He noted that the city, as a government, should find
  ways to better leverage its tax dollars.

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern with the city’s involvement in Chamber of
  Commerce research.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ury, to direct
  staff to survey the local Chambers, consult with the Regional Chamber of Commerce and
  report back to the Council on costs to sustain and maintain Chamber operations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Kelley, Leckness, Ledesma, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT: None

Council Member Kelley

City Council Minutes  10  September 7, 2010
 Mayor Kelley congratulated the Mission Viejo High School Football Team for their win in the
recent Emerald City Classic in Washington State. She noted that representatives of the
Timberline Homeowners Association spoke this evening on behalf of the Turf Lane Park
improvements and when she visited the park the last two Saturdays, she was incredibly
impressed by the work that had been done by city staff, the Boy Scout volunteers, and the
neighbors themselves who came out of their houses and spent time planting. She thanked Mayor
Pro Tem Leckness and City Manager Wilberg for volunteering their own time and one of the
City’s contractors, Nieves Landscape, for providing lunch for the volunteers. Mayor Kelley
discussed her attendance at the Marine car wash fundraiser which had a really good turnout and
the monies will help to support our adopted Marine Battalion. She also announced that she is
hosting a blood drive, at city hall, on Thursday, September 9, 2010, in honor of the 9-11 victims,
and heroes past and present who protect our city and our nation. Mayor Kelley shared the good
news about a Performing Arts Center at Capistrano Valley High School. The CUSD Board of
Trustees voted to go out to bid and the dream is becoming a reality thanks to a $3 million grant
from the State of California with the remaining funds coming from our own Mission Viejo
Mello-Roos dollars. She stated that the current CUSD Board Members are very supportive of
the Performing Arts Center at Capistrano Valley High School and it will be a wonderful addition
to the campus. She reminded residents that CUSD schools will be back in session tomorrow and
Saddleback Valley Unified schools will start next Monday. Mayor Kelley noted that Council
Member Schlicht made a lot of disparaging remarks about the city this evening. To listen to
Council Member Schlicht, one would think that we live in a real rat hole and she asked residents
to really look at the city: it is the safest city in California, the 3rd safest city in the nation, we
have a AAA bond rating, state of the art athletic facilities, more than 50% of general fund
revenues in reserves, staff cut $5 million in 18 months during these difficult economic times and
we are more than matching the decline in revenues. Mayor Kelley stated that she loves her city,
she has raised my children here and it bothers her to hear disparaging remarks about this
wonderful community. Mayor Kelley concluded her comments by announcing that the
Community of Character word for the month of September is responsibility and she reminded
residents that the city hosts free Movies of Character, with Casablanca screening next on
September 19, 2010, in the City Council Chamber.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:15 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting to Monday, September 20, 2010, at 5:00 p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 20, 2010

City Council Minutes  11  September 7, 2010
